analysis.title: Excelerate Energy Inc (EE): 3Q26 Recap: Operational Flexibility Solves Hormuz Risk; Caribbean Expansion Supports Multi-Year Growth Runway
key_insights: EE reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $133.5m, above GSe of $128m and FactSet consensus of $129m (+5%/+4%). Better Terminal Services margins offset slightly softer LNG, Gas, and Power margins versus GS estimates.

EE narrowed FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance to $495-515m (prior $490-515m). GSe is now $508m and consensus $498m. Total capex guidance was lowered to $465-485m (from $465-495m) as higher growth capex was offset by lower maintenance capex.

EE plans to eliminate Strait of Hormuz crossings in 2027 for both its Iraq terminal and Colombia FSRU projects by swapping vessels. Iraq will use an FSRU already in the region instead of the Acadia, with regional LNG supply, and keeps its 2Q27 in-service date. Colombia will use other FSRUs in the fleet instead of the Express, and keeps its 1Q27 in-service date.

Management reiterated project returns despite the vessel swaps: $100m of annual EBITDA on Iraq and a 35% contract uplift on Colombia. GS says the absence of cross-ocean fuel fees may be offset elsewhere in project economics. GS sees the swaps as a proof point on fleet operational flexibility and says Strait of Hormuz transit risk had been a key overhang on the stock.

EE announced the Bahamas LNG Hub, a floating LNG storage and distribution terminal near Grand Bahama, backed by an 11-year agreement with AxDo Bahamas for 16 tbtu/yr of LNG, which is less than half of the asset's capacity. Initial deliveries ramp in 1Q27 through the Jamaica platform for ~$6m of annual EBITDA. A dedicated FSU follows in 2H28 for $15m of annual EBITDA on the AxDo contract alone, with $85-95m of guided capex.

GS expects the Bahamas terminal to reach ~$30m+ of run-rate EBITDA once the remaining capacity is contracted. It supports EE's plan to grow the integrated Caribbean footprint by $80-110m of EBITDA by 2030.

EE signed a five-year extension with Petrobras for the FSRU Sequoia, now through 2038, adding $400m to contracted backlog. A reliquefaction unit will be installed at the 2028 dry dock, giving modest upside to contracted revenue from 2028.

Seatrium was awarded the EPC contract to convert the Methane Patricia Camila LNG carrier into an FSRU. Total project capex rose to ~$260m including the vessel purchase, with management reiterating a 5-7x build multiple. The 2028 in-service date is unchanged. Commercialization of the vessel is the next focus, and EE holds a Seatrium shipyard slot option for another conversion.

Management's building blocks for EBITDA growth by 2029: ~$100m+ from Iraq, ~$10m from the Colombia charter rate step-up, $80-110m from Caribbean expansions, and ~$40-50m from Patricia Camila (~$100m if integrated). GS estimates an 11% EBITDA CAGR for 2025-2030 versus ~7% for its midstream coverage average.

Each incremental FSRU conversion option could add ~6% to GS's 2030 estimates standalone, or ~13% on an integrated basis. GS sees a potential need for ~30-115 mtpa of floating regas capacity additions globally by the mid-2030s, supporting 2-5 FSRU additions to EE's fleet at an unchanged 25% market share.

GS raised EBITDA estimates ~1% on average for 2026-2032 and delayed the start of the Qatar/Petrobangla LNG supply contract, which depends on improved LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz. GS expects low double-digit dividend growth through 2028.
GS reiterates Buy with a $49 12-month price target (unlevered DCF, 10.25% WACC, 3% terminal growth), 38.7% upside from the $35.34 close on 5 Nov 2026. EE rose 3% on the day versus AMNA down 3%.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 adj. EBITDA beat, Hormuz transit risk removed from the 2027 Iraq and Colombia projects through vessel swaps, and new Bahamas and Sequoia contracts extend the growth runway. PT unchanged at $49.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees a supportive environment for regasification infrastructure as new global LNG supply requires downstream regas capacity, with global import demand growth and price-elastic demand supporting additions.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $133.5m vs GSe $128m and FactSet consensus $129m (+5%/+4% beat), reported 5 Nov 2026.
FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance narrowed to $495-515m (prior $490-515m). GSe $508m vs FactSet consensus $498m, both post-print estimates.
FY26 total capex guidance lowered to $465-485m from $465-495m.
GS EBITDA estimates (est.) 2026E $508m, 2027E $581m, 2028E $670m, 2029E $701m, 2030E $761m, 2031E $768m, 2032E $783m. GS says it is ahead of consensus through 2031.
GS EPS estimates (est.): 2026E $1.54 (old $1.41), 2027E $1.69 (old $1.67), 2028E $2.04 (old $2.10). 3Q26 EPS shown in the report table as $0.44 for 9/26.

trade_ideas.rationale: Compelling risk-reward from derisked 2027 growth, industry-leading EBITDA growth and a contracted earnings runway.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher global gas pricing, prolonged Middle East conflict, higher FSRU conversion costs, competition for FSRU deployments, and higher LNG supply costs for Iraq.

risk_factors: Higher global gas pricing could weigh on global LNG demand.
Longer-than-expected geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
Higher-than-expected conversion costs for incremental FSRUs.
Higher-than-expected LNG supply costs for the Iraq project.
Counterparty credit risk and customer FX convertibility risk.
Balance sheet over-extension and/or equity funding needs.

geopolitical: Strait of Hormuz transit risk for EE's Iraq and Colombia FSRU deployments in 2027, addressed through vessel swaps and regional LNG sourcing.

Longer-than-expected geopolitical conflict in the Middle East is listed as a downside risk. The Qatar/Petrobangla LNG supply contract start is delayed pending improved LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
